stimuli.text: Water enters a tank at a rate modeled by $$E(t) = 10 + 5\sin\left(\frac{t}{3}\right)$$ gallons per hour and leaves the tank at a rate modeled by $$L(t) = 6\sqrt{t + 1}$$ gallons per hour, for $$0 \leq t \leq 8$$. At time $$t = 0$$ the tank contains 102 gallons of water.
The curves $$r = 3 + 2\cos\theta$$ and $$r = 4$$ are drawn in the polar plane for $$0 \leq \theta \leq 2\pi$$.
Consider the curve given by $$x^2 + xy + y^2 = 48$$.
Consider the differential equation $$\frac{dy}{dx} = 4x(y - 3)$$. Let $$y = f(x)$$ be the particular solution with $$f(1) = 6$$.

The function $$f$$ is defined by the power series $$f(x) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{n+1}x^n}{n\cdot 4^n} = \frac{x}{4} - \frac{x^2}{2\cdot 16} + \frac{x^3}{3\cdot 64} - \cdots$$ for all $$x$$ in its interval of convergence.

questions.stem: What is $$\int_{-1}^{2} \left(6x^{2} - 6x\right)dx$$?

options.why: This adds F(a) instead of subtracting it.
This is F(b) only; subtract F(a) as well.
Correct. An antiderivative is $$F(x) = 2x^{3} - 3x^{2}$$; $$F(2) - F(-1) = 9$$.
This subtracts values of the integrand instead of an antiderivative.

questions.explanation: By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, $$\int_{-1}^{2} f(x)\,dx = F(2) - F(-1)$$ with $$F(x) = 2x^{3} - 3x^{2}$$. That is $$4 - (-5) = 9$$.

questions.stem: A particle has velocity $$\vec{v}(t) = \langle 2t - 2, 3t^{2} + 2 \rangle$$ and position $$(1, -3)$$ at $$t = 0$$. Where is the particle at $$t = 1$$?

options.why: Correct. Add the integral of each velocity component to the starting coordinate.

questions.stem: If $$f(x) = \tan x$$, what is $$f'\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$$?

This value doesn't come from the correct derivative formula.

questions.explanation: $$\frac{d}{dx}\left(\tan x\right) = \sec^2 x$$. Substituting $$x = \frac{\pi}{4}$$ gives $$2$$.

options.why: This is $$f'(2)$$, the first derivative.
This lowers each exponent twice but only multiplies by the exponent once.
This drops the constant that comes from the quadratic term.

questions.stem: At what value of $$x$$ does the graph of $$f(x) = x^{3} - 3x^{2} - 6x - 3$$ have a point of inflection?

options.why: Correct. $$f''(x) = 6x - 6$$ is zero and changes sign at $$x = 1$$.
This is −b/(2a), the vertex formula for a parabola, applied to the cubic's coefficients. Set f″(x) = 0 instead.
Inflection points are where f″ changes sign, not where f″ has its constant term.
Sign error when solving f″(x) = 0.

questions.explanation: $$f'(x) = 3x^{2} - 6x - 6$$ and $$f''(x) = 6x - 6$$. $$f''$$ is linear, so it changes sign at its zero, $$x = 1$$.

questions.stem: If $$\int_0^{1} f(x)\,dx = 5$$ and $$\int_0^{3} f(x)\,dx = 10$$, what is $$\int_{1}^{3} \left(-f(x) + 2\right)dx$$?

options.why: Correct. $$\int_{1}^{3} f = 10 - (5) = 5$$, so the integral is $$-1(5) + 2(2)$$.
This adds the two given integrals; the integral from a to b is their difference.
This forgets to multiply the integral of $$f$$ by $$-1$$.
The integral of the constant $$2$$ over an interval of length $$2$$ is $$4$$, not $$2$$.

questions.explanation: $$\int_{1}^{3} f(x)\,dx = \int_0^{3} f - \int_0^{1} f = 5$$. By linearity, the requested integral is $$-1 \cdot 5 + 2 \cdot 2 = -1$$.

questions.stem: A twice-differentiable function $$f$$ satisfies $$f'(5) = 0$$ and $$f''(5) = 6$$. Which of the following must be true?

options.text: $$f$$ has a point of inflection at $$x = 5$$.
options.why: f″ is not zero, so this is not a candidate for inflection.

Correct. f′ = 0 and f″ > 0: the graph is concave up at a horizontal tangent.

options.text: There is not enough information to classify $$x = 5$$.
options.why: The second derivative test applies because f″ ≠ 0.

questions.explanation: By the Second Derivative Test, $$f'(c) = 0$$ with $$f''(c) > 0$$ gives a relative minimum.

questions.stem: What is $$\int_0^{\pi/2} \sin(2x)\,dx$$?

options.why: This forgets the factor $$\frac{1}{2}$$ from the inner function.
This makes a sign error in the cosine values; the region is entirely above the axis, so the integral is positive.
The antiderivative of $$\sin u$$ is $$-\cos u$$; this drops the negative sign.

questions.explanation: $$\int \sin(2x)\,dx = -\frac{1}{2}\cos(2x) + C$$. Evaluating: $$-\frac{1}{2}\left[\cos\pi - \cos 0\right] = \frac{2}{2}$$.

questions.stem: Let $$f(x) = \begin{cases} -2x + 1 & x < 2 \\ -x + 4 & x \geq 2 \end{cases}$$. What is $$\lim_{x \to 2^-} f(x)$$?

options.why: Correct. For $$x < 2$$, $$f(x) = -2x + 1$$, which approaches $$-3$$.
This is the right-hand limit (and $$f(2)$$). The left-hand limit uses the formula for $$x < 2$$.
This value doesn't come from substituting the approach point into the left-hand formula.
One-sided limits can exist even when the two-sided limit does not.

questions.explanation: The left-hand limit uses the piece for $$x < 2$$: $$-2(2) + 1 = -3$$.

questions.stem: A population satisfies $$\frac{dP}{dt} = 0.002P(800 - P)$$ with $$P(0) = 40$$. For what value of $$P$$ is the population growing fastest?

options.why: Correct. Half the carrying capacity, where the parabola $$\frac{dP}{dt}$$ in $$P$$ has its maximum.
At the carrying capacity the growth rate is 0.
The initial population is not where growth is fastest.
The maximum of $$P(L - P)$$ is at $$\frac{L}{2}$$.

questions.explanation: $$\frac{dP}{dt} = 0.002P(800 - P)$$ is a downward parabola in $$P$$ with zeros at 0 and 800, so it is largest at $$P = 400$$.

questions.stem: The functions $$f$$, $$g$$, and $$h$$ satisfy $$g(x) \leq f(x) \leq h(x)$$ for all $$x$$, where $$g(x) = 4 - 4(x - 3)^2$$ and $$h(x) = 4 + 4(x - 3)^2$$. What is $$\lim_{x \to 3} f(x)$$?

options.text: It cannot be determined without a formula for $$f$$.
options.why: The Squeeze Theorem determines the limit without a formula for $$f$$, because the bounds share the same limit.
Correct. Both $$g$$ and $$h$$ approach $$4$$ as $$x \to 3$$, so the Squeeze Theorem forces $$f$$ to approach $$4$$ too.
This adds the limits of $$g$$ and $$h$$; the squeeze gives their common value.
This is the input value being approached, not the output.

questions.explanation: $$\lim_{x \to 3} g(x) = 4$$ and $$\lim_{x \to 3} h(x) = 4$$. Since $$f$$ is trapped between them, the Squeeze Theorem gives $$\lim_{x \to 3} f(x) = 4$$.

questions.stem: A particle moves in the plane with $$x'(t) = 2t$$ and $$y'(t) = \frac{3}{4}t^2$$. What is the speed of the particle at $$t = 2$$?

options.why: Speed is the magnitude of the velocity vector, not the sum of its components.
This forgets the square root.
This is the slope of the path, not the speed.

questions.explanation: At $$t = 2$$, $$\vec{v} = \langle 4, 3 \rangle$$, so the speed is $$\sqrt{16 + 9} = 5$$.

questions.stem: Let $$C(x)$$ be the cost, in dollars, of producing x items. Which of the following is the best interpretation of $$C'(3) = -7$$?

options.text: The average rate of change of the cost over the first 3 items is -7 dollars per item.
options.why: The derivative is an instantaneous rate at one input, not an average over an interval.

options.text: The cost when 3 items have been produced is -7.
options.why: This describes $$C(3)$$, the value of the function, not its rate of change.

options.text: The cost changes by -7 over the first 3 items.
options.why: This describes a total change over an interval, which is an integral of the rate, not the derivative at one point.

options.text: The cost is decreasing at a rate of 7 dollars per item when 3 items have been produced.
options.why: Correct. A derivative at a point is an instantaneous rate of change, with units of output per unit of input.

questions.explanation: $$C'(3)$$ is the instantaneous rate of change of $$C$$ when 3 items have been produced. Its sign (negative) says the cost is decreasing, and its units are dollars per item.

questions.stem: What is the sum of $$\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} 7\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)^n$$?

options.why: This divides by $$r$$ instead of $$1 - r$$.
Correct. Geometric with first term $$7$$ and ratio $$\frac{3}{5}$$.
The formula is $$\frac{a}{1 - r}$$, not $$\frac{a}{1 + r}$$.
The first term depends on the starting index; check the term for the first value of n.

questions.explanation: $$|r| = \left|\frac{3}{5}\right| < 1$$, so the series converges to $$\frac{7}{1 - \left(\frac{3}{5}\right)} = \frac{35}{2}$$.

questions.stem: What is the radius of convergence of $$\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{n\,(x - 3)^n}{6^n}$$?

options.why: The series converges for all x only when the ratio limit is 0 for every x.
The center is not the radius.
The radius is the reciprocal of this.
Correct. The ratio test gives $$\frac{|x - 3|}{6} < 1$$.

questions.explanation: $$\left|\frac{(n + 1)(x - 3)^{n+1}}{6^{n+1}}\cdot\frac{6^n}{n(x - 3)^n}\right| = \frac{n + 1}{n}\cdot\frac{|x - 3|}{6} \to \frac{|x - 3|}{6}$$. Convergence needs this below 1, so $$R = 6$$.

questions.stem: What is the coefficient of $$x^{5}$$ in the Maclaurin series for $$f(x) = e^{2x}$$?

questions.stem: A particle moves along the x-axis with velocity $$v(t) = t^{2} - 3t$$, and its position at $$t = 0$$ is $$x(0) = 5$$. What is the position of the particle at $$t = 5$$?

questions.stem: Let $$f(x) = \begin{cases} x^{2} - 4 & x \leq 0 \\ -1 & x > 0 \end{cases}$$. Which of the following is true?

options.why: The one-sided limits differ, so $$f$$ has a jump.

options.text: $$f$$ is neither continuous nor differentiable at $$x = 0$$.
options.why: Correct. The left piece gives $$f(0) = -4$$ with slope $$0$$; the right piece approaches $$-1$$ with slope $$0$$. The one-sided limits differ, so $$f$$ is not continuous, and therefore not differentiable.

options.text: $$f$$ is continuous but not differentiable at $$x = 0$$.
options.why: The one-sided limits differ, so $$f$$ is not continuous.

options.text: $$f$$ is differentiable but not continuous at $$x = 0$$.
options.why: Differentiability implies continuity, so this can never happen.

questions.explanation: The left piece gives $$f(0) = -4$$ with slope $$0$$; the right piece approaches $$-1$$ with slope $$0$$. A jump discontinuity rules out continuity, and a function that isn't continuous at a point can't be differentiable there.

questions.stem: What is the value of $$\int_{2}^{6} f(x)\,dx$$?

questions.stem: An open-top box is made from a 6-inch by 6-inch square of cardboard by cutting equal squares of side $$x$$ from each corner and folding up the sides. What value of $$x$$ gives the box its maximum volume?

questions.stem: The sum of $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{n}$$ is approximated by its first 5 terms. What is the smallest upper bound on the error given by the alternating series error bound?

questions.stem: Let $$y = f(x)$$ be the solution to $$\frac{dy}{dx} = x^2 - y$$ passing through the point $$(1, -2)$$. What is $$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}$$ at that point?

questions.stem:
Which of the following series converge?

I. $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{n}{n^2 + 1}$$

II. $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^n}{\sqrt{n}}$$

III. $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^2}$$

options.why: Check each series with an appropriate test: I diverges, II converges, III converges.
Check each series with an appropriate test: I diverges, II converges, III converges.

questions.explanation: Series I diverges: limit comparison with the harmonic series. Series II converges: alternating series test, but p = 1/2 for the absolute values. Series III converges: p-series with p = 2 > 1.

questions.stem: Let $$P_{2}(x)$$ be the degree-2 Taylor polynomial for $$f$$ about $$x = 2$$, and suppose $$|f^{(3)}(x)| \leq 30$$ for all $$x$$. What is the Lagrange error bound for $$|f(\frac{11}{4}) - P_{2}(\frac{11}{4})|$$?

questions.stem: What is the slope of the line tangent to the polar curve $$r = 4 + \cos\theta$$ at $$\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}$$?

questions.explanation: Replace $$x$$ by $$3x$$ in the series for $$\sin x$$: the $$x^{5}$$ term is $$\frac{(3x)^{5}}{5!}$$, so the coefficient is $$\frac{81}{40}$$.

questions.stem: Let $$P_{4}(x)$$ be the degree-4 Taylor polynomial for $$f$$ about $$x = 2$$, and suppose $$|f^{(5)}(x)| \leq 6$$ for all $$x$$. What is the Lagrange error bound for $$|f(\frac{5}{2}) - P_{4}(\frac{5}{2})|$$?

options.why: The distance from the center must be raised to the power n + 1.
This forgets to divide by $$(n + 1)!$$.
Correct. $$\frac{6}{5!}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{5}$$.
This uses the degree n instead of n + 1 for the factorial and power.

parts.prompt: How many gallons of water enter the tank during the time interval $$0 \leq t \leq 8$$?

rubric.criterion: Writes a definite integral of $$E$$ over the interval.

parts.prompt: Is the amount of water in the tank increasing or decreasing at time $$t = 5$$? Give a reason for your answer.

rubric.criterion: Concludes correctly, with a reason that compares $$E$$ and $$L$$ (or uses the sign of $$E - L$$).
rubric.example: $$E(5) - L(5) \approx 0.280$$, which is positive, so the amount is increasing.

parts.prompt: At what time $$t$$, for $$0 \leq t \leq 8$$, is the amount of water in the tank greatest? Justify your answer.

rubric.criterion: Sets $$E(t) - L(t) = 0$$ to find the critical points.
Evaluates the amount at the critical points and the endpoints (Candidates Test).
Gives the correct time with justification.

parts.prompt: How many gallons of water are in the tank at time $$t = 8$$?

rubric.criterion: Uses the initial amount plus the integral of the net rate.

parts.prompt: Find the area of the region enclosed by $$r = 3 + 2\cos\theta$$.
Find the area of the region inside $$r = 3 + 2\cos\theta$$ and outside $$r = 4$$.

rubric.criterion: Writes outer squared minus inner squared.

parts.prompt: Find $$\frac{dr}{d\theta}$$ at $$\theta = 2$$. Is the curve moving toward or away from the origin at that angle? Explain.

rubric.example: Since $$r > 0$$ and $$\frac{dr}{d\theta} < 0$$, the curve is moving toward the origin.

parts.prompt: Find the slope of the line tangent to $$r = 3 + 2\cos\theta$$ at $$\theta = 2$$.
Find the x-coordinates of all relative extrema of $$f$$, and classify each as a relative maximum or relative minimum. Justify your answer.

rubric.criterion: Classifies both with a sign-change justification.
rubric.example: $$f'$$ changes from positive to negative at $$0$$ (relative maximum) and from negative to positive at $$4$$ (relative minimum).

parts.prompt: On what intervals is the graph of $$f$$ concave down? Give a reason.

rubric.criterion: Gives the interval with a reason based on $$f''$$.

parts.prompt: Find the absolute maximum value of $$f$$ on the closed interval $$[-2, 4]$$. Justify your answer.

rubric.criterion: Evaluates $$f$$ at the critical points and endpoints.

parts.prompt: Find $$\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{f(x) - f(0)}{x^2}$$.

rubric.criterion: Recognizes the form 0/0 and applies L'Hospital's Rule (twice, or once with $$f'(0) = 0$$).

parts.prompt: Show that $$\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{2x + y}{x + 2y}$$.

rubric.criterion: Differentiates implicitly, using the product rule on the $$xy$$ term.
Solves for $$\frac{dy}{dx}$$ to reach the given expression.

parts.prompt: Write an equation for the line tangent to the curve at the point $$(-4, -4)$$.

rubric.criterion: Finds the slope and writes the line.

parts.prompt: Find the coordinates of every point on the curve at which the tangent line is horizontal.

rubric.criterion: Sets the numerator equal to zero.
Substitutes into the curve and solves.

parts.prompt: Find $$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}$$ at the point $$(-4, -4)$$.

rubric.criterion: Differentiates $$\frac{dy}{dx}$$ with the quotient rule, treating $$y$$ as a function of $$x$$.

parts.prompt: Find the slope of the slope-field segment at each of the points $$(-1, 4)$$, $$(0, 5)$$, $$(1, 2)$$ and $$(2, 3)$$.
Write an equation for the line tangent to the graph of $$f$$ at $$x = 1$$, and use it to approximate $$f(1.2)$$.

rubric.criterion: Finds the slope at the point and writes the tangent line.

parts.prompt: Find $$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}$$ in terms of $$x$$ and $$y$$. Is the approximation in part (b) an overestimate or an underestimate? Explain.

rubric.criterion: Uses the sign of the second derivative at the point to conclude.
rubric.example: At $$(1, 6)$$, $$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 60$$, so f is concave up and the tangent line lies below the curve: an underestimate.

parts.prompt: Find the particular solution $$y = f(x)$$ with $$f(1) = 6$$.
Find the interval of convergence of the series. Show the work that leads to your answer.

rubric.criterion: Analyzes both endpoints with a test.
rubric.example: At $$x = 4$$: $$\sum \frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{n}$$ converges (alternating series test). At $$x = -4$$: $$-\sum \frac{1}{n}$$ diverges (harmonic).

parts.prompt: Find the first three nonzero terms and the general term of the Maclaurin series for $$f'(x)$$. Then write $$f'(x)$$ as a rational function.
Use the first two nonzero terms of the series to approximate $$f(1)$$. Show that this approximation differs from $$f(1)$$ by less than $$0.008$$.

rubric.criterion: Uses the alternating series error bound with justification.
rubric.example: The series at $$x = 1$$ alternates with terms decreasing to 0, so the error is at most the third term, $$\frac{1}{3\cdot 64} = \frac{1}{192}$$.
